candidate_relations.reason: Myxoid liposarcoma is a distinct myxoid sarcoma of adipocytic lineage. While it shares a myxoid stroma and can present as a large intramuscular thigh mass, the cytological description here—monotonous cells in cords and single-file arrangement with nuclear grooves in a myxoid background, without lipoblasts—is more consistent with extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma. Myxoid liposarcoma would typically show lipoblasts and a characteristic branching capillary network, which are not described. This is an incompatible subtype, not the reference diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Different myxoid sarcoma subtype; liposarcomatous rather than chondrosarcomatous lineage

candidate_relations.reason: Low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma is a fibroblastic tumor with myxoid and fibrous zones, typically showing bland spindle cells in a whorling pattern. While it can present as a deep soft tissue mass, the cytological features described—monotonous cells forming anastomosing cords and single-file arrangements in a prominent myxoid stroma with nuclear grooves—are more characteristic of extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma. This represents an incompatible subtype relative to the reference diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Different myxoid sarcoma subtype; fibroblastic rather than chondrosarcomatous lineage

case_quality_flags: Cytological features (anastomosing cords, single-file arrangement, nuclear grooves, prominent myxoid stroma, monotonous cells) are classic for extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma; neither candidate captures this entity
